Status: Accepted — implemented in Phase 2 Date: 2026-07-31 Implemented: 2026-07-31

Context

The demo stores JSON blobs in SharedPreferences. Production needs bounded, queryable multi-page feed caching, saved-paper pinning, comment caches, drafts, account-scoped state, schema migrations, transactions, and a durable sync outbox. These cannot be safely managed as a collection of preference blobs.

Decision

Use Drift over SQLite as the mobile content database. It owns relational public cache data, saved-paper projections, comment cache, drafts, cache metadata, and the retry outbox. SharedPreferences remains only for small scalar preferences and selected restoration metadata. Authentication tokens are not stored in Drift; they remain in platform secure storage.

The feed repository remains cache-first and stale-while-revalidate. Drift schema migrations are explicit, public data may be retained across sign-out, and account-owned rows and outbox records are cleared or scoped on sign-out and account deletion.

Implemented shape

The production database uses the stable pakperk_content.sqlite filename and currently has schema version 10. Foreign keys are enabled and the database uses WAL mode. The schema contains:

  • normalized paper, feed-query, and ordered feed-membership tables;
  • generation- and arXiv-version-bound processing, Introduction, Connections, and anonymous chat caches;
  • a bounded comment-page cache; and
  • account-scoped five-state Library, custom-list/tag membership, draft, outbox, sync-state, and cache-metadata tables;
  • generation-bound normalized document/Passport/visual/semantic response caches and position-only reading checkpoints; and
  • account-scoped annotations, retained note-conflict versions, evidence cards, memory items, research outbox/sync state, and version-diff cache entries. All Plan 03 surfaces remain behind default-off build and server flags.

Feed rows are keyed by an opaque, versioned identity that includes the exact category and limit. The first-page validator is stored with that query, while cursor-page appends preserve it. Paper metadata is monotonic by arXiv version and source update time. A newer paper version clears derived rows in the same transaction, and processing-generation changes prevent late Introduction, Connections, or chat responses from crossing a retry boundary.

The one-time legacy importer parses existing feed, paper, processing, Introduction, Connections, and chat blobs with the ordinary model decoders, imports and verifies accepted rows in one transaction, and removes bulk preference keys only after that verification succeeds. A derived record is accepted only when an individually cached paper proves the exact arXiv version, the JSON explicitly carries a positive generation, and the corresponding processing row for that generation was imported first. Chat additionally needs an explicit session, paper, and arXiv envelope matching the exact feed/restored route reader key and the anonymous session that existed when the importer was constructed. It never mints or resamples an identity to label old chat, so genuine unscoped v1 derived/chat blobs fail closed instead of borrowing newer provenance. The marker is committed only while the complete captured bulk snapshot and imported chat session remain unchanged, and cleanup compares each key again before removal. Invalid, wrong-typed, and unbound rows are counted without logging their content. A failed or raced transaction leaves the source preferences in place and does not block startup. Under strict full-text policy, public metadata is masked and all derived legacy records are discarded by policy.

Eviction applies comment expiry, stale non-active feed membership, unpinned paper LRU/TTL, and then expired or oldest unprotected derived generation clusters under byte pressure. It protects the active reader window, restored paper routes and chats, library pins, drafts, and pending outbox ownership. Swipe-time maintenance enforces metadata-row and live SQLite-byte bounds without vacuuming. Physical allocation includes the main database, WAL, and shared-memory files; checkpointing and VACUUM run only during a non-interactive lifecycle state.

FeedPrefetchCoordinator is separate from the screen and receives only a feed-page remote interface plus the Drift persistence capability. Its defaults are centralized (30-row pages, trigger at 10 remaining, 2 behind/6 ahead in the readable window, 60 durable rows ahead, 500 metadata rows, 64 MiB, and a 7-day metadata TTL). Query-local single-flight, snapshot obsolescence, bounded retry, and cursor-cycle termination keep speculative work coherent. The narrowed remote interface makes the no-prepare boundary structural rather than a caller convention.

Consequences

  • The app has generated database code, migration tests, database lifecycle management, bounded cache eviction, and migration from legacy preferences.
  • Feed cache entries become query/category/cursor-aware instead of a single initial-page JSON value.
  • The schema persists idempotent save/unsave operations in an outbox while offline, and Phase 4 owns their guarded synchronization behavior. Public comment drafts remain distinct from the outbox and never auto-publish.
  • Existing cached-first UI behavior is preserved while the data model becomes queryable and transactional.

Security and operational implications

  • SQLite contains no access tokens, refresh tokens, raw authorization material, or account credentials.
  • Account-owned tables are structurally separated for logout/account-switch cleanup and later deletion; public paper metadata can remain available offline.
  • Private research bodies are ordinary SQLite text. This ADR does not claim application-layer database encryption: the current local boundary is the OS app sandbox, device access controls, platform file protection, and backup exclusion/disablement. SQLCipher is deferred until a reviewed threat model defines key ownership, migration, restore/recovery, rotation, and cleanup.
  • Cache size, TTL, LRU eviction, saved-paper pinning, and lifecycle-safe physical compaction have focused metrics and tests.
  • Migrations are explicit and tested from complete historical schema fixtures through version 10. Rebuildable pre-generation derived blobs are discarded during the version-3 migration instead of being relabeled as current. Later migrations add synchronized-library state, account-bound comment caches/drafts and blocks, remove the dormant reply column, add the Plan 02 Library/search/reading-feed projections, then add Plan 03 document and private-research caches without weakening prior boundaries.

状态： 已接受——已在阶段 2 实现 日期： 2026-07-31 实现日期： 2026-07-31

背景

演示版将 JSON 数据块存储在 SharedPreferences 中。生产环境则需要容量有界且可查询的多页 Feed 缓存、对已保存论文的驻留保护、评论缓存、草稿、按账户隔离的状态、schema 迁移、事务，以及持久化的待同步队列（outbox）。这些需求无法作为一组偏好设置数据块安全管理。

决策

使用基于 SQLite 的 Drift 作为移动端内容数据库。它负责关系型公共缓存数据、已保存论文的投影数据、评论缓存、草稿、缓存元数据以及用于重试的待同步队列（outbox）。SharedPreferences 仅用于存储少量标量型偏好设置和选定的恢复元数据。身份认证令牌不存储在 Drift 中，而是继续保存在平台安全存储中。

Feed 仓库继续采用缓存优先策略，并在后台重新验证期间允许返回陈旧缓存。Drift 的 schema 迁移均显式定义；公共数据可以在退出登录后继续保留；在退出登录和删除账户时，账户自有数据行及待同步队列（outbox）记录会被清除，或严格限定在对应账户的作用域内。

已实现的结构

生产数据库使用稳定的文件名 pakperk_content.sqlite，当前 schema 版本为 10。数据库启用了外键并采用 WAL 模式。schema 包含：

  • 规范化的论文表、Feed 查询表和有序 Feed 成员关系表；
  • 与处理代次和 arXiv 版本绑定的处理状态、Introduction、Connections 及匿名聊天缓存；
  • 容量有界的评论页缓存；
  • 按账户隔离的五状态 Library 表，以及自定义列表/标签成员关系、草稿、待同步队列（outbox）、同步状态和缓存元数据表；
  • 与代次绑定的规范化文档、Passport、视觉和语义响应缓存，以及仅记录位置的阅读检查点；
  • 按账户隔离的注释、保留的笔记冲突版本、证据卡片、记忆项、研究待同步队列（outbox）/同步状态和版本差异缓存条目。所有 Plan 03 功能仍受默认关闭的构建开关和服务器开关控制。

Feed 数据行以一个不透明且带版本的标识为键，其中包含确切的类别和条数上限。第一页验证器随对应查询一同存储，追加游标分页时则保留该验证器。论文元数据只会按 arXiv 版本和来源更新时间单调向前更新。较新的论文版本会在同一事务中清除派生数据行；处理代次发生变化时，则会阻止迟到的 Introduction、Connections 或聊天响应越过重试边界写入。

一次性旧版导入器使用常规模型解码器解析现有的 Feed、论文、处理状态、Introduction、Connections 和聊天 JSON 数据块，在同一事务中导入并验证符合条件的数据行，并且只在验证成功后删除批量偏好设置键。只有同时满足以下条件时，导入器才接受派生记录：单独缓存的论文能够证明完全一致的 arXiv 版本；JSON 明确携带正数代次；该代次对应的处理状态行已先完成导入。对于聊天数据，还必须有显式的会话/论文/arXiv 封装，并且它既要匹配来自 Feed 或恢复路由的确切阅读器键，也要匹配导入器构造时已经存在的匿名会话。导入器绝不会生成或重新采样身份标识来标注旧聊天；因此，导入器会在作用域校验失败时默认拒绝确实不带作用域信息的 v1 派生数据块和聊天数据块，而不会借用较新的溯源信息。只有当捕获的完整批量快照和已导入的聊天会话均保持不变时，才会提交迁移完成标记；清理时还会在删除前再次比较每个键。无效、类型错误或未绑定的数据行只会计数，不会记录其内容。失败或发生竞态的事务会保留源偏好设置，并且不会阻塞启动。在严格的全文策略下，公共元数据会被遮蔽，所有旧版派生记录都会按策略丢弃。

淘汰过程依次处理过期评论、陈旧且非活跃的 Feed 成员关系，并依据 LRU/TTL 淘汰未固定的论文；最后仅在字节容量存在压力时，淘汰已过期或最旧且不受保护的派生代次簇。它会保护当前活跃的阅读器窗口、已恢复的论文路由和聊天、Library 中已固定的论文、草稿，以及待同步队列（outbox）中待处理记录的所有权关系。滑动操作期间的维护不会执行数据库收缩，但会强制遵守元数据行数和 SQLite 当前占用字节数的上限。物理分配量包括主数据库文件、WAL 文件和共享内存文件；检查点操作和 VACUUM 仅在生命周期处于非交互状态时运行。

FeedPrefetchCoordinator 与界面分离，只接收 Feed 页面远程接口和 Drift 持久化能力。其默认值集中定义：远程页面每页 30 行，在剩余 10 项时触发；可读窗口在当前位置之前保留 2 项、之后保留 6 项；前方持久化 60 行；元数据上限为 500 行；数据库容量上限为 64 MiB；元数据 TTL 为 7 天。每个查询内的合并并发机制、快照失效判定、有界重试和游标循环终止机制共同保证推测性预取工作的一致性。收窄后的远程接口使“不得触发论文准备”成为结构边界，而不只是调用方需要遵守的约定。

后果

  • 应用包含数据库生成代码、迁移测试、数据库生命周期管理、有界缓存淘汰机制，以及从旧版偏好设置迁移的逻辑。
  • Feed 缓存条目能够区分查询、类别和游标，不再只是单个首页 JSON 值。
  • 数据库 schema 会在离线时将幂等的保存/取消保存操作持久化到待同步队列（outbox）中，其受保护的同步行为由阶段 4 负责。公共评论草稿始终与待同步队列（outbox）分离，绝不会自动发布。
  • 在数据模型变得可查询且支持事务的同时，现有的缓存优先 UI 行为得以保留。

安全与运维影响

  • SQLite 不包含访问令牌、刷新令牌、原始授权材料或账户凭据。
  • 账户自有表在结构上单独划分，以便退出登录或切换账户时进行清理，并支持后续删除；公共论文元数据可以继续离线使用。
  • 私有研究正文以普通 SQLite 文本形式存储。本 ADR 不声称提供应用层数据库加密：当前的本地安全边界由操作系统应用沙盒、设备访问控制、平台文件保护，以及备份排除或禁用机制共同构成。暂缓引入 SQLCipher，直至经过审查的威胁模型明确密钥所有权、迁移、备份还原/故障恢复、轮换和清理方案。
  • 缓存大小、TTL、LRU 淘汰、已保存论文的驻留保护，以及生命周期安全的物理压缩均有专项指标和测试。
  • 数据库迁移均显式定义，并使用完整的历史数据库模式测试夹具完成截至版本 10 的迁移测试。 在版本 3 迁移期间，会丢弃不含代次信息且可重建的派生数据块，而不会将其重新标记为当前数据。后续迁移依次添加 Library 同步状态、与账户绑定的评论缓存/草稿和屏蔽关系，移除已停用的回复列，添加 Plan 02 的 Library/搜索/阅读 Feed 投影，再添加 Plan 03 的文档缓存和私有研究缓存，同时不削弱此前建立的边界。
